chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: The Kirby sextet's quality and the Barnet battle at the 1939 World's Fair
summary: Leeman praises the band's impeccable musicians and Shavers's difficult book, recalling the Kirby group nearly outswinging Barnet's 16 pieces with O'Neil Spencer on drums.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: We was just talking about John Kirby and that fantastic band -- and I don't think any other small band has ever come up to that reputation, the biggest little band in the land, John Kirby, with that fabulous group, of which you had at one time been a member of one of the groups -- maybe one or two of the groups, with Cliff Leeman, which you had once been a member.

Before me, the band was comprised of impeccable musicians, Buster Bailey's thoroughly -- because Charlie Shavers wrote a book that was pretty rough to play, and they played impeccably. Every member. By the same token, Billy Kyle fed that band, and I played against them with Charlie Barnet, doing the Worlds Fair in '39, and
they almost cut us a brand new one, and I had never seen their drummer.

O'Niel Spencer -- who fed them double time -- the thing with the fast wrists, and he and Charlie Shaver, they almost blew Charlie Barnet 's 16 pieces -- we had four trombones, and four or five trumpets then, and you should have heard them out swing us at certain points.
